allowed_origins.description: The Origin headers browsers may connect from (e.g. https://app.example.com); empty: any. Clients that send no Origin (not browsers) aren't affected.
allowed_origins.title: Allowed origins

asyncapi.description: The API to serve: an AsyncAPI 3.0 or 3.1 document, as JSON or YAML text, or as an object. The channels of its receive operations are the WebSocket paths (their addresses), and their messages' JSON Schema payloads type and validate what clients send. It must be self-contained (no external $refs).
asyncapi.title: AsyncAPI document

auth.description: none, bearer (Authorization: Bearer <token>), api_key (a header or query parameter) or mtls (client certificates).
auth.title: Authentication

auth_secrets.description: bearer and api_key: {"label": "secret"}. The label of the one a request used becomes its event's principal.
auth_secrets.title: Tokens / keys

enqueue_timeout_ms.description: How long a message waits for the workflow to take it (messages are read one at a time, so a slow workflow slows the client down); then the connection closes with 1013 (try again later).
enqueue_timeout_ms.title: Enqueue timeout (ms)

h2c.description: Without TLS: accept HTTP/2 with prior knowledge besides HTTP/1.1.
h2c.title: Cleartext HTTP/2

header_allowlist.description: The only request headers events carry (wins over the denylist).
header_allowlist.title: Header allowlist

header_denylist.description: Request headers events never carry. Default: authorization, proxy-authorization, cookie, set-cookie, x-api-key (and the API key's header).
header_denylist.title: Header denylist

invalid_messages.description: A message no definition of its channel takes (not JSON, or its payload schema fails): drop it (a WARN once a minute), or close the connection (1008).
invalid_messages.title: Invalid messages

h2_max_send_buf_bytes.description: HTTP/2: what one stream may have waiting to be sent before its writer waits. Memory per stream with slow readers (e.g. SSE subscribers): with 1 000 HTTP/2 SSE subscribers, 4 KiB gave ~3x the throughput and a fifth of the memory of 64 KiB, at ~10 % less for a single fast stream.

listen.description: Address and port. Anything but loopback needs auth (or auth: none set explicitly).
listen.title: Listen on

max_message_bytes.description: A larger message (or frame) closes the connection (1009).
max_message_bytes.title: Largest message (bytes)

mtls_allow.description: mtls: SHA-256 fingerprints or names (SAN DNS / URI, or CN). Empty: any certificate the client CA signed.
mtls_allow.title: Allowed client certificates

out_schema.description: Set by the plugin's configurator from the document: the common message fields and channels["<address>"].{path_params, messages.<name>}.
out_schema.title: Out schema (derived)

paths.description: Without a document: the paths clients connect to (default ["/ws"]); every message is an event, as bytes.
paths.title: Paths

ping_interval_s.description: The server pings each client this often; a client that has sent nothing since the last ping is closed.
ping_interval_s.title: Ping interval (s)

read_buffer_bytes.description: Per connection, allocated up front (tungstenite's default is 128 KiB): smaller saves memory with many clients, and larger messages just take more reads.
read_buffer_bytes.title: Read buffer (bytes)

subprotocols.description: The subprotocols the server speaks (Sec-WebSocket-Protocol), in order of preference; a client offering none of them still connects, without one.
subprotocols.title: Subprotocols

tls_cert.description: Uploaded PEM file: the server's certificate chain. Turns TLS on (HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1 by ALPN).
tls_cert.title: TLS certificate

tls_client_auth.description: With a client CA: optional or required (required for auth: mtls).
tls_client_auth.title: Client certificates

tls_client_ca.description: Uploaded PEM file: the CA(s) of client certificates (mTLS).
tls_client_ca.title: Client CA

tls_key.description: Uploaded PEM file: the server's private key.
tls_key.title: TLS key
